title: Reviewing: Keeping Your System Functional
coreMove: Refresh your system until every reminder is complete, current, and safe to trust again

exampleSpecs.domain: a charge nurse doing a Friday afternoon review of staffing notes, supply requests, and follow-up calls
exampleSpecs.audience: a hospital shift lead whose week leaves scraps of commitments in pockets, texts, and handoff sheets
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a promised equipment request and two staff callbacks vanish into memory until they become interruptions during patient care
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse identifies that the miss came from an unreviewed holding place, then repairs the review routine instead of blaming herself for not remembering

exampleSpecs.domain: a public defender scanning active case folders before Monday court
exampleSpecs.audience: an overextended lawyer carrying dozens of small promises across hearings, clients, clerks, and investigators
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a client update, interpreter request, or evidence follow-up is current before the week starts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the example must show the case list becoming trustworthy only after each matter is checked for outcome, next action, waiting-for item, and calendar trigger

exampleSpecs.domain: a parent coordinating a ninth grader's sports forms, orthodontist appointments, and shared custody logistics
exampleSpecs.audience: a household captain who feels ambushed by school emails and family obligations
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether family commitments keep surfacing as bedtime anxiety instead of sitting in clear reminders
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the parent notices that relief comes not from finishing everything, but from seeing the full family map and deciding what is not being done this week on purpose

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school band director reviewing festival deadlines after rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher managing students, buses, permission slips, instrument repairs, and administrator requests
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the concert season is run from a current inventory or from whoever asks loudest that day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the dialogue must have the director separate calendar-only deadlines from next-action list items and waiting-for reminders during the review

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance translator returning from a three-day trip with receipts, client notes, and half-answered messages
exampleSpecs.audience: an independent contractor who has no assistant and no clean boundary between travel, billing, and client delivery
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether unpaid invoices and promised revisions stay hidden in travel debris until cash flow or reputation suffers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the scene must linger on gathering all loose inputs first, then reviewing lists so the system becomes whole before new work is chosen

exampleSpecs.domain: a community theater stage manager one week before opening night
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer coordinator juggling props, actors, venue rules, and last-minute fixes
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether rehearsal energy gets spent on real next moves or on rediscovering the same unresolved issues each night
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the stage manager uses the review to close loops by updating project statuses, deleting stale reminders, and surfacing the few actions that actually belong at tonight's rehearsal

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional maintenance supervisor reviewing open repair tickets across six apartment buildings
exampleSpecs.audience: a field manager moving between sites with phone calls, vendor promises, tenant complaints, and inspection dates
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether urgent-looking messages crowd out older safety, compliance, and waiting-for items that still matter
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor chooses the review before jumping into the newest complaint, proving that current lists make later priority decisions calmer and more accurate
